meta.w5_note: W5 (window-level mixed model) is implemented in a separate module and is deliberately not imported here
meta.aggregation: window -> filing (unweighted mean over that filing's windows of the analysed section) -> firm (unweighted mean over the firm's filings) -> tier
meta.failed_window_rule: any_failed windows are DROPPED, never imputed (ANALYSIS_PLAN.md s8 rule 1)
meta.usability_gate_note: the ANALYSIS_PLAN.md s8 rule 2 gate (>= 2 surviving windows AND >= half surviving) governs the PRIMARY pipeline and is applied there by aggregate_to_firm.  The battery's variants deliberately do not re-apply it, because W4(ii) is defined to leave a 2-window filing with 1 window and W7(i) is defined to exclude tails; re-gating would silently narrow the sensitivity checks.  Each variant reports its own filing and firm counts, and W7(i) also reports the gradient with the gate applied.

primary.gradient_definition: firm-level small-cap mean minus large-cap mean; this is the signed quantity W2/W3/W4/W6/W7 are defined on
primary.tier_trend_statistic_note: the ordered-trend (Jonckheere-Terpstra) statistic returned by analysis.trend_tests.tier_trend_statistic; non-negative, hence not usable as a signed gradient

2-3.identification_note: NOT IDENTIFIED for a three-tier comparison - missing tier(s): mid

9+.identification_note: NOT IDENTIFIED for a three-tier comparison - missing tier(s): small

coarsened_exact_matching.estimand: ATT-style weighted Small-minus-Large, weights = n_small per stratum

W2.criterion: the primary sign must not be CONTRADICTED (reversed with a CI excluding 0) in any bin containing all three tiers
W2.criterion_note: evaluated on 2 bin(s) containing all three tiers

W3.criterion: the primary sign must hold in >= 90% of k = 2 draws

k=2.restriction: every filing (k equals the sample minimum)

k=4.restriction: filings with at least 4 surviving windows
k=4.criterion_note: the pre-declared >= 90% criterion is defined on k = 2 only; this row is reported for information

first_2_windows.note: windows with chunk_index < 2 in every filing

excluding_first_window.note: all windows except each section's first (chunk_index >= 1)
excluding_first_window.note_on_dropout: a 2-window filing contributes 1 window here; a 1-window section contributes 0 and the filing drops out entirely

held_fixed: the filing -> firm -> tier structure and tier sizes
the pooled empirical distribution of window-level disagreement
the pre-registered window -> filing -> firm -> tier aggregation
randomised: which pooled value lands in which window (i.i.d., with replacement)
and therefore all tier, firm and filing signal in the measure
W6.interpretation: the 95th percentile of the null gradient is the largest Small-minus-Large difference that unequal window counts alone manufacture 5% of the time

exact_windows_only.note: only windows of exactly 1200 words (tail-merged windows excluded)
exact_windows_only.gate_note: MIN_USABLE_CHUNKS = 2. These filings are RETAINED in the W7(i) recomputation and reported, so the sensitivity check is not quietly narrowed; the pre-registered gate governs the primary pipeline, and W7(i) is a sensitivity analysis of it.

word_count_covariate_ols.se_note: classical SEs are the pre-registered 'simple OLS'; firm-clustered SEs are reported beside them because windows are nested in filings in firms and classical SEs understate uncertainty
word_count_covariate_ols.specification: embedding_disagreement_window ~ 1 + tier_mid + tier_small + log(word_count); reference tier = large; unit = window

gate.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN.md s5: the tier result is reported as SUPPORTED only if it passes W3 and W5 and is not contradicted in an overlapping W2 bin
gate.verdict_pending_W5: NOT ROBUST TO WINDOW COUNT on the battery's own tests - ANALYSIS_PLAN.md s7 clause 2 applies
